description: Polymeric PTC Resettable Fuse 60V 3A Through Hole P=10.2mm
designVerdict: DROPPED - superseded by the 10 A connector and the size target
notes: DROPPED from the design. Specified when the module connector was 3 A (Wurth WR-PHD); the move to picoMAX at 10 A puts the worst case at 28% of rating and removes most of its job. It is also through-hole radial - 192 mm2 for the pair, and mass on leads in a vibration environment. Kept on record in case a later revision wants per-channel fusing.
60 V max, 3 A hold, 6 A trip, 8 s max time to trip, 40 mOhm at 25 C (80 mOhm post trip). 48k stock, $0.16.

Chosen over a fuse because a blown fuse means a dead channel until a spare is found, and PPTC trip time in seconds matches how a connector actually fails - thermally, slowly. It resets itself once the fault is removed.

WHAT IT PROTECTS AGAINST: gross overload - a shorted cable, a channel stuck at full output. Trip is 6 A against a 3 A hold, so behaviour between 3 A and 6 A is indeterminate and depends on ambient and duration. It will NOT reliably catch a marginal 3.2 A sustained overload, which is the realistic software-bug case; that stays the job of the predictive per-channel limit and the thermal cap.
Insertion loss at the balanced 2.43 A per channel: 0.24 W and 0.10 V, which is 0.27% of a 36 V bus. Negligible.

THROUGH-HOLE, 10.2 mm pitch. The 60 V SMD PPTCs top out near 0.5 A hold - voltage and current trade off directly in this technology, so there is no SMD option at 3 A/60 V. Two through-hole parts is either a small JLCPCB assembly surcharge or two joints by hand.
